::: {#exr-miller-int-by-parts-gaussian}
#### Integration by parts with an exponential factor

Evaluate the integral:

$$\int_a^b x^3 \exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}\,dx$$
:::

::: {#sol-miller-int-by-parts-gaussian}
Factor the integrand as $x^2 \cd \paren{x \exp{-x^2/2}}$. Set:

$$u = x^2, \qquad dv = x\exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}\,dx$$

Then $du = 2x\,dx$ and $v = -\exp{-x^2/2}$.

Using integration by parts ($\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du$):

$$\ba
\int_a^b x^3 \exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}\,dx &= \sb{-x^2 \exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}}_a^b - \int_a^b \sb{-\exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}}(2x\,dx)
\\
&= \sb{-x^2 \exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}}_a^b + 2\int_a^b x\exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}\,dx
\\
&= \sb{-x^2 \exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}}_a^b + 2\sb{-\exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}}_a^b
\\
&= \sb{-(x^2 + 2)\exp{-\frac{x^2}{2}}}_a^b
\\
&= (a^2 + 2)\exp{-\frac{a^2}{2}} - (b^2 + 2)\exp{-\frac{b^2}{2}}
\ea$$
:::
